Lessons.Title: Expressed in Different Ways
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: demonstrate equivalence of exponent expressions representing the same growth over different period groupings (monthly, annual and multi-year), and justify correct change of time units. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of This first-party Edulytiks material follows the reviewed local Algebra 1 learning objectives and uses independently authored examples.

Original hypothetical indicator starts at100 units and grows1% per month. After36 months, expression A=100(1.01)^36. Grouped into three complete years of12 months, this equals100((1.01)^12)^3, with effective per-year factor (1.01)^12≈1.126825. Both expressions are exactly equivalent before rounding the annual factor.

Equivalent grouping across two half-years of6 months each is100((1.01)^6)^6 for36 months, while100((1.01)^6)^3 describes18 months and is not equivalent. Be precise about exponent multiplication (b^p)^q=b^(pq). A monthly factor raised to12 is an annual multiplier, not an annual *percentage* without subtracting1.

Student task: match six original expressions with time durations, create a counterexample to a wrong regrouping and compare exact expressions against prematurely rounded approximations. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for grouping identity, correct period interpretation, sensible handling of approximations and clear justification of expression equivalence.

First-party Cool-down (teacher-scored): Compare 5*2^(2t) with 5*4^t at t=3 and explain algebraically why they always match; discuss how changing time units affects the expression. Numeric responses supported by the mapped exact families may be auto-checked; the teacher scores symbolic equivalence, time-unit conversions and contextual meaning.

KeyConcepts.Title: Power of a power
KeyConcepts.Definition: (b^p)^q=b^(pq) for a positive base in these models.

KeyConcepts.Title: Time-unit conversion
KeyConcepts.Definition: Monthly periods must be grouped consistently into years or half-years.

KeyConcepts.Title: Exact versus approximate factor
KeyConcepts.Definition: Keep exact grouped expression when checking equality; rounding may break exactness.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Approximate only after applying power rule.
